Implemented numeric `sysctl -n kern.boottime` uptime collection in the FreeBSD (also DragonFly), NetBSD, and OpenBSD hardware collectors. The shared sysctl parser now accepts `=`, `:`, and whitespace delimiters, preserves continuation lines, warns on malformed lines, and warns/returns an empty mapping on command failure.

- `PYTHONPATH=lib:test pytest -q test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py test/units/module_utils/facts/hardware test/units/module_utils/facts/network/test_generic_bsd.py`: 30 passed.

diff --git a/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..46b4a24
--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/units/module_utils/facts/test_sysctl.py
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+from __future__ import (absolute_import, division, print_function)
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+import errno
+
+import pytest
+
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl import get_sysctl, get_uptime_facts
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.freebsd import FreeBSDHardware
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.netbsd import NetBSDHardware
+from ansible.module_utils.facts.hardware.openbsd import OpenBSDHardware
+
+
+def test_sysctl_parses_mixed_formats_and_continuations(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, 'hw.ncpu=4\nkern.osrelease: 7.0\n'
+                                       'machdep.cpu 8\n  continued\nbadline\n'
+                                       'hw.model: CPU\n', '')
+
+    result = get_sysctl(module, ['hw', 'kern'])
+
+    assert result == {'hw.ncpu': '4', 'kern.osrelease': '7.0',
+                      'machdep.cpu': '8\n  continued', 'hw.model': 'CPU'}
+    module.warn.assert_called_once()
+    assert module.warn.call_args[0][0].startswith('Unable to split sysctl line (badline): ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure', [(1, '', 'permission denied'),
+                                     OSError('command failed'), IOError('read failed')])
+def test_sysctl_command_failure_warns_and_returns_empty(mocker, failure):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    if isinstance(failure, tuple):
+        module.run_command.return_value = failure
+    else:
+        module.run_command.side_effect = failure
+
+    assert get_sysctl(module, ['hw']) == {}
+    assert module.warn.call_args[0][0].startswith('Unable to read sysctl: ')
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('hardware', [FreeBSDHardware, NetBSDHardware, OpenBSDHardware])
+def test_bsd_uptime(hardware, mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = (0, '1000\n', '')
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=2000)
+
+    assert hardware(module).get_uptime_facts() == {'uptime_seconds': 1000}
+    module.run_command.assert_called_once_with(['/sbin/sysctl', '-n', 'kern.boottime'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('response', [(1, '1000', 'failed'), (0, '', ''),
+                                      (0, '{ sec = 1000 }', ''), (0, 'not a number', '')])
+def test_invalid_uptime_is_omitted(mocker, response):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.return_value = response
+    assert get_uptime_facts(module) == {}
+
+
+def test_missing_sysctl_raises_value_error(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+
+def test_openbsd_populate_keeps_all_fact_sources(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = [(0, 'hw.ncpu=1\n', ''), (0, '1000', '')]
+    hardware = OpenBSDHardware(module)
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_processor_facts', return_value={'processor': ['CPU']})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_memory_facts', return_value={'memtotal_mb': 512})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_device_facts', return_value={'devices': ['sd0']})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_dmi_facts', return_value={'product_name': 'host'})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_mount_facts', return_value={'mounts': []})
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=2000)
+
+    assert hardware.populate() == {'processor': ['CPU'], 'memtotal_mb': 512,
+                                   'devices': ['sd0'], 'product_name': 'host',
+                                   'mounts': [], 'uptime_seconds': 1000}

+def test_invalid_uptime_is_omitted(mocker, response):

+def test_missing_sysctl_raises_value_error(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = None
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)
+
+    module.get_bin_path.side_effect = None
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = OSError(errno.ENOENT, 'missing')
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        get_uptime_facts(module)

+def test_openbsd_populate_keeps_all_fact_sources(mocker):
+    module = mocker.Mock()
+    module.get_bin_path.return_value = '/sbin/sysctl'
+    module.run_command.side_effect = [(0, 'hw.ncpu=1\n', ''), (0, '1000', '')]
+    hardware = OpenBSDHardware(module)
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_processor_facts', return_value={'processor': ['CPU']})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_memory_facts', return_value={'memtotal_mb': 512})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_device_facts', return_value={'devices': ['sd0']})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_dmi_facts', return_value={'product_name': 'host'})
+    mocker.patch.object(hardware, 'get_mount_facts', return_value={'mounts': []})
+    mocker.patch('ansible.module_utils.facts.sysctl.time.time', return_value=2000)
+
+    assert hardware.populate() == {'processor': ['CPU'], 'memtotal_mb': 512,
+                                   'devices': ['sd0'], 'product_name': 'host',
+                                   'mounts': [], 'uptime_seconds': 1000}
